genre: Elder Scrolls -- Third Era Tamriel (d20 chassis), Glenumbra, High Rock

campaign_rules.voice: Same measured, anthropological Le Guin-adjacent cadence as the wider Glenumbra table -- custom explained through its cost, not named outright; violence stated plainly, its aftermath lingered on.
campaign_rules.premise: Third Era Tamriel, same year and region as The Unquiet Peace (3E 248, Glenumbra/High Rock) but a wholly separate, unconnected thread: Ancar Montclair is a Breton raised as a ward of Camlorn's Chapterhouse of the Eight, Level 0, no class, no magic, no combat training -- a Postulant doing cloister chores. He is meant to become an Inquisitor of the Vigil: heavy armor, shield, one-handed steel, and Restoration/Warding magic, hunting the undead, Daedra-touched, necromancers, and vampires. Every piece of that is earned in fiction, never granted free (ruleset.json Signature System 2, the Vigil's Ascent).
campaign_rules.rules_mode: D&D 5e chassis by explicit player request, Elder Scrolls flavor throughout -- never named in generic D&D terms. Magicka replaces spell slots. Nothing magical or martial exists at character creation. Full ruleset in ruleset.json -- read before running any mechanic.
campaign_rules.death_and_dying: Standard 5e shape: 0 HP = unconscious + death saves (DC 10 Endurance). 3 successes stable, 3 failures dead. Nat 20 = 1 HP, conscious. Nat 1 = 2 failures. Damage at or above max HP in one hit = instant death. At Level 0 this PC has roughly 8 HP and is genuinely fragile -- telegraph real danger before it lands.
campaign_rules.connection_note: Runs parallel to and unconnected from Sits-in-Shadow's story (The Unquiet Peace) and Cassius Aurelinus's (Dragonguard of the Falling Empire) -- shares only the broader world/geography, not plot, NPCs, or location, unless the player deliberately steers there.
